research_mode: official Home Office crime-outcomes technical annex only; outcome definitions, timing, transfer, validation and comparability gates; no parcel result or local-risk score claimed

sources.name: Outcomes framework discretion purpose
verified_claims: The outcomes framework is intended to recognise a range of disposals without treating one outcome as universally better than another.
limitations: Outcome categories must not be ranked as a simple performance league table.

sources.name: Alternative-offence outcome rule
verified_claims: Outcome types 1A, 2A and 3A record charges or cautions for an offence different from the offence originally recorded.
limitations: The specific alternative offence cannot be inferred from the original offence category alone.

sources.name: Detection-to-outcomes framework break
verified_claims: The pre-April-2013 detections regime and later outcomes frameworks use different category structures.
limitations: Historical detections and modern outcomes are not directly interchangeable.

sources.name: Recorded-period cohort method
verified_claims: The recorded-period method follows offences recorded in a period and tracks their outcomes over time.
limitations: Early snapshots contain unresolved cases and are not final cohort distributions.

sources.name: Closed-investigation period method
verified_claims: The closed-period method counts outcomes assigned in the year regardless of when the associated crime was recorded.
limitations: It mixes offences recorded in different years and is not a same-cohort clearance rate.

sources.name: Illustrative rate over 100 percent
verified_claims: Outcomes assigned in a year divided by crimes recorded that year can exceed 100 percent for low-volume crime types because the populations differ.
limitations: Such ratios are illustrative activity measures, not probabilities or true cohort rates.

sources.name: Outcome timeliness proxy
verified_claims: Timeliness measures elapsed time from offence recording to outcome assignment and can be used only as a proxy for investigative efficiency.
limitations: The annex states it should not be considered a firm efficiency measure.

sources.name: Outcome system-recording delay
verified_claims: An operational outcome can be actioned before it is entered on the crime-recording system.
limitations: Recorded assignment time can overstate operational decision time.

sources.name: Transferred-record definition
verified_claims: A transferred record is a crime recorded by one force and passed to another because it occurred outside the first force's jurisdiction.
limitations: Transfer volume can reflect geography and recording practice rather than data quality alone.

sources.name: Cancellation after verifiable information
verified_claims: One cancellation category applies when additional verifiable information determines that no notifiable crime occurred.
limitations: A cancellation must not be interpreted as proof that no incident occurred.

sources.name: Duplicate-record cancellation
verified_claims: A recorded crime can be cancelled because it duplicates or forms part of another crime already recorded.
limitations: Cancellation does not remove the underlying incident from every related record.

sources.name: Transfer and cancellation timing
verified_claims: Transferred or cancelled records are counted in the financial year when the transfer or cancellation occurs.
limitations: Their reporting year may differ from the original offence-recording year.

sources.name: Pre-2016 transfer comparison boundary
verified_claims: Full comparison of the five transfer and cancellation reasons is available only for recent years after March 2016.
limitations: Earlier years can be compared only using the combined category.

sources.name: Transfer force-comparison caution
verified_claims: High or low transfer and cancellation volumes should not automatically be interpreted positively or negatively across forces.
limitations: Local recording timing and jurisdiction patterns can create differences.

sources.name: Twenty-four-hour crime-recording rule
verified_claims: Home Office Counting Rules require recording at the earliest opportunity and at most within 24 hours after the decision to record.
limitations: Faster initial recording can increase later transfers or cancellations and must be considered in comparisons.

sources.name: Crimsec outcome-month convention
verified_claims: On aggregated Crimsec4 returns, an outcome is recorded in the month it is applied, not the month of the original offence.
limitations: Monthly outcome and offence volumes do not describe the same case cohort.

sources.name: Mixed outcomes collection systems
verified_claims: Most forces provide record-level Home Office Data Hub data while remaining coverage is supplemented by manual returns.
limitations: Collection route and submission date can differ by force.

sources.name: Monthly outcomes validation checks
verified_claims: Home Office analysts check unusual changes, obsolete offence classifications and incompatible outcome assignments and return queries to forces.
limitations: Validation reduces but does not eliminate recording error.

sources.name: Corrected-record supersession
verified_claims: For Data Hub forces, corrected record versions supersede the original versions after validation issues are resolved.
limitations: Extracts from different dates can therefore contain different versions of the same record.

sources.name: Force outcome-mix comparison boundary
verified_claims: Outcome mixes differ with force policy, offence composition and community context, so direct force comparisons can be misleading.
limitations: Outcome percentages must not be interpreted as standalone force effectiveness or parcel safety scores.
